tables.label: Table 1
tables.caption: The amino acid sequences of the peptide derivatives and their corresponding physicochemical characteristics
footnotes: a aa, number of amino acids
b Theoretical MW, molecular weight calculated by https://aps.unmc.edu/prediction
c Measured MW, molecular weight (g/mol) determined by mass spectroscopy (MS)
e <µH>, hydrophobic moment obtained from the website: http://heliquest.ipmc.cnrs.fr/
f Pho%, the percentage of hydrophobic residues

tables.label: Table 2
tables.caption: The activities of peptide derivatives against S. epidermidis biofilm
footnotes: a MBIC50 and b MBIC90, are defined as the minimum concentration of peptide that can inhibit biofilm formation more than 50% and 90%, respectively

tables.label: Table 3
tables.caption: The antibacterial activities (MIC and MBC values) of peptide derivatives against both gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria
footnotes: a ATCC, the American Type Culture Collection
b MT strain, bacterial strain provided from Department of Medical Technology, Faculty of Allied Health Sciences, Thammasat University

c MHC, minimum hemolytic concentration, indicated the peptide concentration causing 10% hemolysis of hRBCs. When no 10% hemolysis was detected at 250 µg/mL, a value of 500 µg/mL was used to calculate the therapeutic index. When no 10% hemolysis was observed at a concentration of 0.98 µg/mL, a value of 0.49 µg/mL was utilized for calculating the therapeutic index
d GM + and f GM-, the geometric mean of MIC values from all gram-positive and -negative bacterial strains, respectively
e TI + and g TI-, therapeutic index is the ratio of the MHC to the geometric mean of MICs from all gram-positive and -negative bacterial strains, respectively
